minutes.headline: Committee gave the architects guidance on the new town hall design; no design vote was taken, and staff feedback is pending.
minutes.summary: Taylor and Burns presented revised program adjacencies, floor plans, exterior sketches and a 3D model for a new town hall connected to the Ritter building, with the school offices in the Ritter building and a renovated meeting house. Members and the public discussed the Ritter front entrance, the Massachusetts Avenue facade, the superintendent's window, the Ritter lift versus an elevator, and the crosswalk. The architects will return with options. Staff feedback meetings are set for Wednesday, and two sets of minutes were approved by roll call.

public_comment.topic: Chair asked for public comment at the start of the meeting; none was offered.

public_comment.stated_role: member of the public (also School Committee, speaking as public)
public_comment.topic: Asked about the Ritter elevator, offices without windows versus records and vault on exterior walls, distance to the road, and executive session space. Said the plan is rambling and needs aggressive signage, wanted event bathroom access, and said it lacks a strong town-hall architectural feature.

public_comment.stated_role: member of the public (Amanda, also a select board member)
public_comment.topic: Suggested stone-block seating instead of stairs at the Ritter front, supported the plans, and agreed another sidewalk or crosswalk on Mass Ave is not feasible.
Supported large stone blocks as seating where the Ritter steps were.
Thanked the committee and said she was impressed by how the group works together.

votes.motion: Approve the minutes of December 2 (roll call: Allison, Roy, Gray, Scullin-Brini, Leon and Midus aye; Blat's answer on this set was unclear)
Approve the minutes of December 16 (roll call: Allison, Gray, Leon, Scullin-Brini and Midus aye; Roy and Blat abstain)
Adjourn (roll call: Allison, Roy, Gray, Leon, Scullin-Brini, Blat and Midus aye, plus the chair)

budget_items.topic: New town hall footprint and cost
budget_items.what_was_said: The architect said the new town hall is about 20% larger than the last version and he is concerned about how that will show up in the budget.
The chair recalled that renovating the previous building would have committed roughly $30 million, which led to widening the charge to all municipal buildings.

budget_items.topic: Cost of treatment at the Ritter front
budget_items.what_was_said: A member warned that extras such as a terrace add cost and that a high number could be rejected by the town. Another suggested showing a green space as an add alternate.
The chair estimated the cost of an elevator shaft and the architect guessed lower. The committee asked for cost analysis of a lift versus a full elevator.
The architect referred to a figure of roughly $15 million for the project.

decisions.decision: The chair noted Dave's three points (stairs at the Ritter front, the superintendent window, prominence of the School Street entrance) to carry into the group discussion.
Straw poll: no committee interest in creating an actual entrance at the historic Ritter front. Members want something done there, not an entrance.
Architects are to return with several options for treating the former Ritter stair location (pseudo-stairs, plantings, landscaping, seating). The committee agreed.
The majority wants a prominent facade facing Mass Ave, preferring the arch design without the wraparound porch.
The committee is split on the superintendent window, and it will get staff input. The majority favors replacement, with the architect offering aesthetic options.
The architects will analyze the cost of a lift versus a full elevator in the Ritter building.
The chair and members agreed the crosswalk should stay in its existing location.
The next meeting is Wednesday, January 22, at 5:30 pm. Renderings are due February 3 and go to the select board on February 4.

what_happened.line: The committee gave the architects design guidance on a new town hall joined to the Ritter building; no design vote was taken and options are to come back.
A straw poll showed no committee interest in a real entrance at the historic Ritter front; members want that spot treated some other way.
A majority favored a prominent Mass Ave facade, preferring the arch design without the wraparound porch.
The committee split on the superintendent window; staff input will be sought, and the architects will price a lift against a full elevator in Ritter.
The next meeting is Wednesday, January 22, at 5:30 pm; renderings are due February 3 and go to the select board on February 4.

why_it_matters: The architect said the new town hall has grown compared with the last version and raised concern about how that shows in the budget, so the size of the building is tied to what a future town vote may be asked to fund.
Choices still open, such as the lift or elevator and the treatment at the Ritter front, change the cost the town would be asked to approve.
